messages.subject: transforming scales discretely
parts:
Dear all,

It is often interesting when displaying time series to put emphasis on
the display of more recent figures. This is often done by using, for
example 3/4 of the horizontal space with one scale (displaying for
example the time series over the last few years, excluding observation
from the last month) and 1/4 with a "higher" frequency (displaying the
series over the last month). This permits to contemplate both the
more recent movements in more detail as well as to keep this movements
"in perspective". If this possible in ggplot2, possibly transforming
the time scale somehow? Many thanks in advance for your help.
Kind regards,
Ivan

messages.author: 599a13812d4cd3e8
messages.subject: Re: transforming scales discretely
parts:
I see what you are saying (hey, the reply-to worked too :)

I'd sometimes like to be able to do this too, I graph events and
sometimes they come fast and furious, and I've thought about
stretching time in those sections.

I can't quite get my head around what would make a sensible
interface. Eventually time series are turned into X-Y plots and the
breaks/labels are applied (think of the X axis actually being a large
count, like seconds since 1970 or something similar). So you'd want
to specify parts of the time-series where the spaces on the X axis
represented different periods of time (i.e. numbers of seconds), and
then get the labels right as well. To do this in any arbitrary manner
seems pretty tough to me.

Perhaps one could provide an array of breaks, each being a date, and
then communicate that you wanted those to be equally spaced on the X
axis (e.g. "2007-01-01, 2007-02-01, 2007-03-01, 2007-04-01,
2007-04-02, 2007-04-03, ...). The method, something like a
specialized subset, would then need to make a new XY graph, with the
appropriate values for those dates taken from the data-frame, and that
set of labels. Seems like that could be written externally to
ggplot2, just passing in the new series not as a Date series, though.

A similar transformation is when you are plotting financial (or other
data) when you want to remove weekends and public holidays. I've done
this a few times by converting the dates to numeric, munging them in
some way, and then adding a custom continuous scale with appropriate
breaks and labels. I've never figured out a good generalisation
(instead doing the transformation "by hand" each time), but this would
be very useful.
